screening.reason: Inclusion 2-3: analyses a large ABIDE I+II resting-state fMRI discovery sample for sex-by-diagnosis group-difference connectivity, replicated in independent samples.

ABIDE I and II dataset of N = 1019 included N = 82 
females with autism, N = 362 males with autism, N = 166

evidence_spans.claim: Cases were selected aged 7-18 years with successful registration, FIQ 70-148, and mFD within 3xIQR+Q3 of the sample (~0.39mm).

evidence_spans.text:
At each step, any sites with less than three individual 
datasets per diagnostic/sex groups were excluded.
evidence_spans.claim: Sites with fewer than three individual datasets per diagnostic/sex group were excluded.

evidence_spans.text:
R-fMRI image pre-processing 
steps included: slice time correction, 24 motion param-
eters regression [57], component-based noise reduction 
(CompCor) [58], removal of linear and quadratic trends, 
and band-pass filtering (0.01–0.1 Hz, for all metrics but

evidence_spans.claim: R-fMRI preprocessing included slice-time correction, 24-motion-parameter regression, CompCor noise reduction, detrending, and band-pass filtering; five metrics examined: PCC-iFC, VMHC, ReHo, DC, fALFF.

evidence_spans.text:
To account for site and collection time variability 
across each of the data collections in ABIDE I and II data 
repositories, site effects were removed using the ComBat 
function available in python [61] (https​://githu​b.com/
brent​p/comba​t.py). This approach has been shown to 
effectively account for scanner-related variance
evidence_spans.claim: Site effects across ABIDE I and II data collections were removed using the ComBat harmonisation function.

evidence_spans.text:
Discovery analyses in ABIDE revealed significant main effects of diagnosis and sex across the intrinsic func‑

ity (VMHC) in several cortical regions, largely converging in the default network midline.
evidence_spans.claim: Discovery analyses in ABIDE showed significant main effects of diagnosis and sex on PCC-iFC, ReHo and VMHC converging on the default network midline.

evidence_spans.text:
Sex-by-diagnosis interactions

assessments.support: Age, FIQ, registration success, mFD and site-minimum-N exclusion rules explicitly stated, with full details cross-referenced to Supplementary Methods.
N by diagnosis and sex, and 13 sites, are reported, with per-site/per-measure missingness tabulated (Table 1).
Preprocessing pipeline steps explicitly described (slice-timing, motion regression, CompCor, band-pass filter, registration) and tested for robustness to alternative pipelines.
ADI-R/ADOS-based phenotypic variables are referenced (Table 1 footnotes) but the diagnostic confirmation procedure itself is not restated in the main extracted text.
Age and mFD matched across groups; site modeled; sex and diagnosis are the primary factors of interest.
Site harmonised via ComBat; age and mFD included as nuisance covariates in the GLM.
Five established R-fMRI metrics (PCC-iFC, VMHC, ReHo, DC, fALFF) used, each validated in prior literature.
Voxel-level Z>3.1 and cluster-level P<0.01 threshold set to account for five R-fMRI metrics tested (Bonferroni-equivalent 0.05/5).

risk_of_bias.summary: Large, well-documented ABIDE I+II discovery sample with explicit QC/exclusion rules, ComBat site harmonisation, robustness checks across preprocessing pipelines, and replication in two independent cohorts; main gap is that the diagnosis-confirmation method is not restated in the main text.

charting.title: Towards robust and replicable sex differences in the intrinsic brain function of autism
charting.authors: Dorothea L. Floris; José O. A. Filho; Meng-Chuan Lai; et al.
charting.primary_focus: Sex-by-diagnosis differences in intrinsic brain function
charting.primary_goal: Characterise robust and replicable sex differences and sex-by-diagnosis interactions in resting-state brain function in autism
charting.country_region: Multi-site (13 merged sites from ABIDE I and II)
charting.diagnosis_assessment: ADI-R and ADOS-2 scores available as phenotypic variables (per Table 1 footnotes); confirmation procedure not restated in main text
charting.dataset_openly_available: Yes — ABIDE I and II data freely accessible via the FCP-INDI repository
charting.specific_features: PCC-seed intrinsic functional connectivity (iFC), voxel-mirrored homotopic connectivity (VMHC), regional homogeneity (ReHo), degree centrality (DC), fractional ALFF (fALFF); Harvard-Oxford atlas used for anatomical labelling of clusters
charting.feature_extraction_tools: Custom R-fMRI pipeline (slice-timing correction, 24-parameter motion regression, CompCor, detrending, band-pass filtering, FSL FLIRT BBR + ANTs registration); C-PAC credited in author contributions for analyses support; ComBat (python, brentp/combat.py) for site harmonisation
charting.feature_change_direction: Sex-by-diagnosis interaction: reduced VMHC in autistic females vs. increased/typical VMHC pattern in the other three groups, localized to dorsolateral occipital cortex
charting.validation_methodology: Voxel-level GLM (Z>3.1, cluster-level P<0.01, GRF-corrected); robustness checked across alternative preprocessing pipelines; replication tested in two independent cohorts (EU-AIMS LEAP, GENDAAR)
charting.summary_key_findings: In the ABIDE I+II discovery sample (N=1019, 13 sites), main effects of diagnosis and sex were found across PCC-iFC, ReHo and VMHC converging on the default-network midline; a sex-by-diagnosis interaction on VMHC in dorsolateral occipital cortex showed reduced VMHC in autistic females and replicated in the larger of two independent cohorts (EU-AIMS LEAP) but not GENDAAR.
charting.features_associated_disorder: PCC-iFC, ReHo and VMHC group differences along the default-network midline; VMHC sex-by-diagnosis interaction in dorsolateral occipital cortex
charting.future_directions_recommended: A priori harmonisation across discovery and replication datasets; systematic study of sample-related factors affecting replicability.
charting.reviewer_notes: ABIDE I and II data collections explicitly merged by matched site (e.g., KKI & ABIDEII-KKI1) to form 13 combined sites for ComBat harmonisation.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational) voxel-wise R-fMRI study; ABIDE I+II discovery sample, N=1019 (82 F ASD, 362 M ASD, 166 NT F, 409 NT M) across 13 merged sites; replicated in EU-AIMS LEAP and GENDAAR.
narrative_row.methods: Custom R-fMRI preprocessing (slice-timing, motion regression, CompCor, band-pass filter, BBR+ANTs registration) with ComBat site harmonisation; five metrics (PCC-iFC, VMHC, ReHo, DC, fALFF) analysed via voxel-wise GLM with diagnosis, sex and their interaction as regressors, age and mFD as covariates.
narrative_row.outcomes: Main effects of diagnosis and sex converged on the default-network midline across PCC-iFC, ReHo and VMHC; a sex-by-diagnosis interaction on VMHC in dorsolateral occipital cortex (reduced VMHC in autistic females) replicated in EU-AIMS LEAP but not GENDAAR.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Lack of a priori harmonisation among discovery and replication datasets; diagnosis-confirmation method not restated in main text; replicability varied by metric and sample.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Large, methodologically transparent use of combined ABIDE I+II data with explicit QC thresholds, ComBat site harmonisation, and independent-sample replication — a strong example of reconstructible cohort definition.

kg_link.cohort_description: N=1019 (82 F ASD, 362 M ASD, 166 NT F, 409 NT M) selected from ABIDE I and II, aggregated across 13 merged sites; inclusion: age 7-18, successful registration, FIQ 70-148, mFD within 3xIQR+Q3 (~0.39mm); sites with <3 datasets per diagnostic/sex group excluded.
kg_link.pipeline: Custom (slice-timing, 24-parameter motion regression, CompCor, band-pass filter, BBR+ANTs registration) + ComBat site harmonisation
kg_link.finding: Main effects of diagnosis and sex on PCC-iFC, ReHo and VMHC converged on the default-network midline; a VMHC sex-by-diagnosis interaction in dorsolateral occipital cortex (reduced VMHC in autistic females) replicated in EU-AIMS LEAP but not GENDAAR.
